about: Narrative eval cases. Entries are selected deterministically from the default synthetic ledger by ledgerlens.narrative_eval.select_cases; the expectations below were written by hand from each entry's own lines and flags, never from a model's output. Regexes are case-insensitive and are matched over the whole note. Confidence bands say where a careful reviewer would put the entry; the note is graded on properties, not on similarity to any reference text.

generator.ledger: generate_ledger() defaults: 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31, 10 entries/day, anomaly_rate 0.015, seed 20260922

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as round_amount
cases.notes: $25,000 exactly, from cash into Miscellaneous Expense, 'adjustment per management', keyed by an approver. A round management adjustment to a catch-all account is worth a document; the note should ask for the basis, not assume one.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as weekend_entry
cases.notes: Three tests but $359.08: a Saturday manual revenue credit at month end by a non-approver. Cut-off is the question; the small amount argues for medium, the High test for high. Either is defensible; low is not.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as after_hours_entry
cases.notes: 23:02 posting clearing payables to cash by a non-approver. Unusual hour, ordinary accounts. The note should ask about the user's working pattern, not treat the hour as evidence of anything.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as holiday_entry
cases.notes: Labor Day receipt of $231.34 keyed by the controller. One Medium test, an approver, a trivial amount.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as period_end_manual_revenue
cases.notes: The AU-C 240 pattern: a manual revenue accrual on the last Saturday of the period. The note must ask for cut-off support. Accruals are routine, which is why medium is also acceptable.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as just_under_threshold
cases.notes: $9,950.44 of consulting fees, 0.5% under the $10,000 approval limit, keyed by a non-approver. The note should name the threshold and ask for related invoices from the same vendor.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as duplicate_entry
cases.notes: Same amount, accounts and description as JE-2025-005057 three days earlier, and posted on a Saturday from the AP subledger. The earlier entry's id is the fact that makes the evidence request specific.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as rare_account_pair
cases.notes: A debit to Owner's Equity against cash, described as a reclassification, by a non-approver: the only such pairing in two years. Equity movements need an authorising document.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as dormant_account
cases.notes: A cash refund booked to Sales Returns, a pairing seen once in the population. A credit note or refund authorisation settles it.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as benford_drift
cases.notes: Injected as Benford drift, which no per-entry test can see; only the access-list test fired. To a reviewer this is an ordinary contractor repair keyed by someone off the approver list. The note should say so.

cases.why_chosen: highest-risk flagged entry injected as unbalanced_entry
cases.notes: Debits and credits differ by $143.57 on a suspense clearing into a dormant catch-all account by a non-approver. Either a control failed or the extract is wrong; the note should say the extract is the first thing to confirm.

cases.why_chosen: several tests fired on one entry; the note has to weigh them
cases.notes: $10,000 exactly, to an account dormant for 305 days, 'adjustment per management', by the controller. Two Medium tests that reinforce each other.

cases.why_chosen: several tests fired on one entry; the note has to weigh them
cases.notes: An unbalanced entry for $70.86 against $65.06. Tiny, but an out-of-balance posting is structural: it should not be possible, whatever the size. The note should not let the amount talk it down to low.

cases.why_chosen: several tests fired on one entry; the note has to weigh them
cases.notes: A Saturday marketing payment by a non-approver. Two weak signals; a single enquiry to the user resolves it.

cases.why_chosen: an ordinary entry only the access-list test caught; the note should say the innocent reading is more likely
cases.notes: A cost-of-sales posting for invoice 7061. Nothing about the entry is unusual; the only question is why this user keys manual entries at all, and that is an access question, not an entry question.

cases.why_chosen: an ordinary entry only the access-list test caught; the note should say the innocent reading is more likely
cases.notes: Same shape as JE-2024-000115 with a different user and amount. Rule 5 in the system prompt exists for exactly these: an auditor's time is the scarce resource.
